## Findings ledger
- [C1.DOC1.F2] The source treats AUKUS as having two substantive components: Pillar I on Australia’s acquisition of nuclear-powered submarines and Pillar II on advanced military capabilities and industrial collaboration — dim: case_identity — anchor: "the key plank of AUKUS is contained within ‘Pillar I’ of the agreement, which focuses on supporting Australia to acquire its first nuclear-powered submarines" — doc: aukus — case: AUKUS — object-time-scope: agreement’s Pillar I; Australian nuclear-powered submarines; Pillar II covers advanced military capabilities and collaboration — criterion: shared question of which policy objects and activities define the case — confidence: high Additional support uses anchor-b: "Within ‘Pillar II’ of the agreement is the aim to develop a range of advanced military capabilities, in areas such as quantum technologies, cybersecurity, hypersonic missiles, and artificial intelligence." — doc-b: aukus
- [C1.DOC1.F3] The source extends its analysis beyond the three AUKUS members to Japan and South Korea as non-member states and key defence partners connected particularly to Pillar II — dim: case_identity — anchor: "Our analysis is not only limited to AUKUS member states, but also extends to Japan and South Korea." — doc: aukus — case: AUKUS-plus analytical extension — object-time-scope: AUKUS member states plus Japan and South Korea; analysis of Pillar II and related defence-industrial relations — criterion: analyst-proposed comparison criterion: degree and form of participation by non-member partners, relevant because the source explicitly includes them in its case boundary — confidence: high Additional support uses anchor-b: "Japan and South Korea—two key defence partners under Pillar II" — doc-b: aukus
- [C1.DOC1.F4] The source identifies states, political parties, government agencies, defence contractors, civilian firms, start-ups, venture capital, research institutions, and security apparatuses as actors within or connected to the AUKUS case — dim: case_identity — anchor: "These groups include civilian-run enterprises, defence contractors, state-owned enterprises, and emerging tech start-ups whose interests are represented through a territorial conception of ad hoc coalitions bound by a vision of what a rules-based international order should look like." — doc: aukus — case: AUKUS — object-time-scope: actors linked to AUKUS’s political-economic and security architecture, especially Pillar II — criterion: shared question of which actors belong to the case, relevant for comparing institutional and political-economic composition — confidence: high Additional support uses anchor-b: "Such forces include the market and the state, political coalitions, technology and capital, emerging business groups and key industries, as well as security apparatuses." — doc-b: aukus

scope_outcomes.criterion: The source must identify a documented case or conceptual approach, its boundaries, actors, object, place, time, or justified comparison criteria.
scope_outcomes.basis: The source explicitly defines AUKUS, its three member states, Pillars I and II, its temporal starting point, associated states Japan and South Korea, participating and affected actors, and a militarised-neoliberalism criterion for analysis.
limitations: Japan and South Korea are treated as extensions or partners rather than AUKUS members.
The source does not provide a systematic selection rule for all associated cases or actors.
The inspected article does not define a single closing date for the case.
